rationale: The spec grid (pair_screen_window in [180, 365, 730]) produces 0 viable trades. At w=180 and w=730 no pairs pass the EG p<0.10 test; at w=365 two pairs pass ADF (BTCUSDT-ETHUSDT, ETHUSDT-SOLUSDT) but their AR(1) half-life is INFINITY, so the halflife filter (cap in [10,20,60,120]) rejects all of them (spurious cointegration: ADF passes, OU half-life does not exist). The relaxed diagnostic grid shows the strategy has positive mean OOS Sharpe (best: 2.12 at w=90, entry=1.5, exit=0.5) and positive DSR (1.95), but fails the worst-fold >= 0 gate (best worst = -0.039) and the min_trades_per_fold=30 gate (best min = 6). The 30 trades/fold requirement is structurally infeasible at 1d with this signal density (~150-220 total trades across 2.2y of data). The strategy has edge but does not satisfy the spec's gates - KILL is the honest verdict.

root_cause_no_trades: pair_screen_window=180: trailing 180d shows NO pairs cointegrated at p<0.10 (best p=0.33)
pair_screen_window=365: BTCUSDT-ETHUSDT (p=0.0024) and ETHUSDT-SOLUSDT (p=0.0081) pass ADF but half_life=inf -> spurious cointegration, halflife filter rejects them
pair_screen_window=730: trailing 730d (essentially the entire dataset) shows NO pairs cointegrated at p<0.10 (best p=0.18)

relaxed_grid_diagnostic.interpretation: The strategy has real edge at non-spec windows (mean OOS Sharpe 1.06-2.12, DSR 0.92-1.95 across the relaxed grid). The issue's gates require a signal density and stability that this 1d pairs strategy cannot deliver on a 2.2y dataset. The gates are calibrated for higher-frequency or longer-sample strategies. Per the issue's accepted KILL clause, no params chosen.
